correctness.rationale: Reconstructed inclusion W(N_S)⊆conv σ(N), giving disk radius ≤2A/P. The angle-bisector argument makes p_i=(z_i-c)^2/Π_{j≠i}(z_i-z_j) positive, quadratic Lagrange interpolation gives ∑p_i=1 and det(wI-D_{n⊥})=(w-c)^2. Therefore the 2×2 compression has a centered disk numerical range. Side-supported vectors sqrt(p_j)e_i−sqrt(p_i)e_j place a numerical-range point on each side, forcing radius r. Any maximizing elliptical numerical range contains the unique inball and touches all three triangle sides; a nonnegative degree-2 trigonometric polynomial on the inball circle has three double zeros, hence is identically zero, forcing the disk. Three spectral projections suffice in infinite dimensions. Independent 200 seeded random noncollinear triangle reconstructions checked p_i>0, ∑p_i=1, squared nilpotent part zero, disk radius r; finite diagnostic does not prove general theorem. The finite-matrix positive-block formula relies on Sababheh's pre-existing Φ(X)=δ₂(X), not an independent proof here.

value.rationale: The three-point case is the first genuinely noncollinear spectral regime for normal operators. final_claim: For a bounded normal operator with three noncollinear spectral points, the maximal 2-dimensional-compression elliptical width is 4A/P, attained by the spectral-triangle incircle, and every maximizing numerical-range set is that disk; collinear spectra have zero width; positive-block identity is cited only in finite dimension.
limitations: Exactly three noncollinear spectral points for positive width, all three multiplicities nonzero; no >3-point general spectral formula.
